lead.t: The Absolute Non-Indication: Elevated serum urea or creatinine *alone* is never an absolute indication for emergency dialysis without a clinical or physiological complication (AEIOU).

snip.t: The Absolute Non-Indication: Elevated serum urea or creatinine *alone* is never an absolute indication for emergency dialysis without a clinical or physiological complication (AEIOU).
Her serum urea nitrogen is 15 mg/dL with creatinine of 1.1 mg/dL.
His serum urea nitrogen is 17 mg/dL with creatinine 1.0 mg/dL.
Laboratory studies show her serum urea nitrogen is 52 mg/dL with creatinine 5.3 mg/dL.
| Serum urea & creatinine | Detects renal dysfunction causing toxicity or acidosis | Hyperkalaemia induces sine waves, blocks, arrest |
| Serum urea & creatinine | Renal etiology | Uremia indicates uremic pericarditis requiring urgent renal replacement therapy |

Key investigations include serum electrolytes (especially potassium), serum urea and creatinine (to assess renal function), complete blood count (for anaemia), urinalysis (for protein, blood, casts), and renal ultrasound (to assess kidney size and rule out obstruction).
| Serum urea (BUN) | Nitrogenous waste load | BUN > 100 mg/dl supports uremic indication |
